open_points.subject: installation.resolve_service_credential vs service_invoker.prepare_request failure mode
open_points.text: `public_op:installation.resolve_service_credential` Errors: "`refused` with `credential_unresolved` when the reference does not resolve." / `public_op:service_invoker.prepare_request` Errors: "None: a pre-send failure is a result with its detail from the closed set."
open_points.question: When credential resolution fails during request preparation, is that surfaced as a refusal from `installation.resolve_service_credential`, or as a non-refusal pre-send failure result returned by `prepare_request`?
options: `resolve_service_credential` refuses; `prepare_request` must catch/map that refusal to its result channel
`resolve_service_credential` never refuses; it returns success-or-failure as a result object and `prepare_request` forwards it
open_points.default_guess: Make `prepare_request` always return a non-refusal pre-send failure result (`credential_unresolved`), and treat raw refusal from `installation` as internal_error only if unmapped.

open_points.subject: Run answer schema consistency across runs.read_run and runs.release_run
open_points.text: Conventions: "A run's answer, wherever an operation returns one, holds: `run_id`, the flow version, status, starter and times, outputs produced, waiting points ..." / `public_op:runs.release_run` Outputs: "The run's answer with `released_by` and `released_at`."
open_points.question: Are `released_by` and `released_at` part of the standard run-answer schema everywhere (including `runs.read_run`, `get_run`, `list_records` on runs), or only appended by `runs.release_run`?
options: Include `released_by`/`released_at` in all run answers when present
open_points.default_guess: Include them in all run answers whenever present on the Run record.

open_points.subject: Result shape of non-refusal check operations
open_points.text: Examples: `fit_port_value` Outputs: "Fits, or the first failing check..."; `check_request_shape` Outputs: "Fits, or the first failing rule."; `prepare_request` Outputs: "... or the first pre-send failure..."; `send_prepared_request` Outputs: "One outcome name ..."
open_points.question: What exact machine-readable result format (discriminator fields/enums/detail fields) must these operations return so callers can branch deterministically without parsing prose?
options: Tagged union with explicit enum status + structured detail code + location fields
open_points.default_guess: Use tagged unions with closed enums and structured detail fields.

open_points.subject: store.read_records relation call signatures
open_points.text: "A call names the relation and passes the records its name mentions ... A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and answers `internal_error`."
open_points.question: For each relation in "Relations of `store.read_records`", what is the exact required argument list and field names (including optional/forbidden args), so invalid-shape calls are determined uniformly?
options: Define one explicit input schema per relation
Use one generic map and validate ad hoc per implementation
open_points.default_guess: Define explicit per-relation argument schemas and reject anything else uniformly.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances service iteration domain
open_points.text: `public_op:bindings.check_installed_instances` Errors: "`refused` naming the first failing service, services taken in `service_id` code-point order..."
open_points.question: Which services are included in that ordered set: all services present in installation credentials, all with selected instances, union of both, or another set?
options: Iterate services that have selected instances
Iterate services that have credentials configured
Iterate union of configured service entries
open_points.default_guess: Iterate the union of service entries configured in installation for instance/credential, ordered by `service_id`.
